data.why: OpenDose ships a built-in example project (dose-response/clinical examples plus every assay example) loaded in-browser via the ?example=1 query parameter or the start screen's 'example project' card; no external files are needed to exercise curve fitting and biostatistics.

goals: fit a dose-response curve (4PL/5PL) to a plate-reader assay and read off IC50/EC50 with its confidence interval
run standard-curve/ELISA back-calculation of unknown concentrations with LLOQ/ULOQ and acceptance criteria
compare two fitted curves (e.g. potency ratio of EC50) between a treatment and a control
analyze qPCR Cq data into fold-changes with reference-gene QC and asymmetric confidence intervals
run a one-way ANOVA or t test on column data with multiple-comparisons correction and get a publication-style results sentence
produce a Kaplan-Meier survival curve with log-rank test and hazard ratio from a clinical/animal survival dataset

review.summary: The tree has the right overall shape for a Prism-like biostatistics workspace, and its cited screens mostly match what it says, with honest notes that the Pyodide engine never loaded. But because the engine never loaded, every plan goal stops at set-up rather than a computed result, reporting/export and several core analyses are missing, and one finding (no 5PL in the picker) is a side effect of the broken engine, so it needs a re-run with the engine working plus the listed changes before filing.
